request: Mirror the part according to the plane lying on the not rounded end of the part. Merge the mirrored part together with the existing one so they create one body.

actions.relational_constraint: Use the plane lying on the non-rounded end of the part as the mirror plane.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the non-rounded end of the part and resolve the plane located on that end, including whether it is an existing datum plane or a planar end face.
steps: Select the complete existing solid SOLID 0, including the elongated lever arm section R01 and the blind-bore boss section R02, as the geometry to be mirrored.
Resolve the requested non-rounded end as feature F003, the distal arm end interface. Its B-rep face is FACE 7, a rectangular planar face at CAD x=80 spanning y=11 to 23 and z=2 to 6.
Use the plane coincident with FACE 7 as the mirror plane. This plane is normal to the CAD X-axis and is distinct from the rounded proximal termination F002 represented by cylindrical FACE 0.
Create a full-body mirror transformation across the plane x=80. For implementation, reflect every point of SOLID 0 using x'=160-x while retaining y and z.

Mirror the entire connected solid rather than mirroring only F003 or only the web. The mirrored result must therefore include counterparts of F001 through F006, including the rounded termination, boss, blind bore, and boss-to-arm transition.

Retain the original solid while creating the mirrored solid. The original distal FACE 7 and the corresponding terminal face of the mirrored web must occupy the same plane and share the complete 12 mm by 4 mm interface.

Do not create a new sketch, extrusion, cut, fillet, or chamfer for this operation; use a geometric body-mirror feature so that all existing surfaces and the blind-bore topology are reproduced consistently.

Check the mirrored geometry for validity and confirm that it extends from the mirror plane toward positive CAD X, placing the mirrored boss center at x=160 while the original boss remains centered at x=0.

actions.operation: Merge the mirrored part with the existing part using a Boolean union
actions.target: The mirrored part created by the preceding action and the existing original part
actions.relational_constraint: The mirrored and existing parts must be joined into a single body.
actions.unresolved_reference: Identify the existing original body and the mirrored result, and verify that their geometry permits a single merged body.
steps: Use original SOLID 0 as the Boolean base body and the full mirrored result from the preceding action as the Boolean tool body.

Verify that the two bodies meet over the planar interface defined by original feature F003 and FACE 7 at x=80. The coincident terminal faces provide the required full-area contact for joining the two arm webs.
Perform a Boolean union or fuse operation between the original and mirrored solids with glue or tolerance handling enabled if required for coincident coplanar faces.
Remove the coincident internal interface corresponding to FACE 7 during the union so the joined arm is represented as continuous material rather than two bodies sharing a retained partition face.
Refine or clean the fused B-rep to remove redundant coplanar seam edges and duplicate vertices at x=80 without changing the external dimensions or feature geometry.

Preserve both boss assemblies and both blind bores. In particular, retain the original bore faces FACE 3 and FACE 4 and their mirrored counterparts; the union must not fill, extend, or convert either blind bore into a through-hole.

Preserve the rounded proximal termination F002, the new mirrored rounded termination, and both boss-to-arm blends derived from F006. Do not add fillets or chamfers at the central union because the requested interface is a continuous straight web.
Validate the final result as exactly one connected solid body. Confirm that no separate mirrored solid remains and that the merged body is continuous through the former FACE 7 interface.

intention: Produce one unified body from the original part and its mirrored copy.
